stories.title: Rizwan, Shan, Saim among notable omissions as PCB awards contracts to 38 players
summary: Players on Test-only contracts, however, would be encouraged to prioritise four-day cricket if taking up additional playing commitments.
Existing incentives include doubled match fees for victories against higher-ranked opponents and half the Test match fee for contracted players appearing in domestic four-day cricket.
Players awarded central contracts Test and ODI: Babar Azam, Salman Ali Agha.

stories.title: FM Dar calls for multilateralism, says bloc or unilateral politics will not work
summary: Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar stressed the importance of multilateralism, saying bloc politics and unilateralism would not work.
The foreign minister said that even during the previous round of indirect talks between the US and Iran in Oman, it had been agreed that Pakistan must be present if direct talks were held.
Dar also hailed the June 18 signing of the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding between the US and Iran, but regretted the subsequent violations. “Pakistan hasn’t given up.

stories.title: Musadik Malik holds separate meetings with Iranian, Tajik officials on SCO forum sidelines
summary: Dr Malik arrived at Purana Qila in New Delhi for the second day of the inaugural SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum, according to a post shared by his office earlier in the day.

In a separate meeting with President of Iran’s Islamic Culture and Relations Organisation Mohammad Mahdi Imanipour, Dr Malik underscored the deep-rooted historical and cultural bonds between Pakistan and Iran.

A day earlier, after arriving in New Delhi, Dr Malik had described the forum as a “tremendous opportunity” for multilateral dialogue, saying that cultures and civilisations transcended geographical boundaries.

stories.title: Internet provider expects submarine cable repairs to be completed by Dec 6
summary: Internet service provider Transworld Associates has said repair work on an affected international submarine cable is expected to be completed by December 6, with users likely to experience slower internet speeds during peak hours until the work is finished.

The development follows an earlier announcement by the Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA) that a fault had been reported in the SEA-ME-WE 5 (SMW5) international submarine cable system, approximately 11 kilometres from Pakistan’s coast.
Internet monitoring organisation NetBlocks had also reported a decline in connectivity in Pakistan, saying the incident was consistent with a fault in the SMW5 international subsea cable system.

stories.title: Chinaman or doosra
summary: The other is our ‘all-weather friend,’ and though its political and governance model is completely different, the powers that be would be tempted to emulate it for two reasons.
It seems we may now be tempted to emulate the Chinese political system that produced one of the greatest military-industrial powers.

In our haste to put things right, let’s not forget that the Chinese, among other things, are masters at biding their time because they have internalised their 5,000 years of history, whereas we have actively disowned ours.

stories.title: FBI, US Agriculture Department breached by hackers: reports
summary: The US Agriculture Department and the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) were breached by hackers in cyberattacks, US media reported on Saturday, as concerns deepened over the recent spate of tech outages at key American institutions.
The US Department of Agriculture (USDA) told employees that a system used to facilitate payments to farmers was targeted in a cyberattack, NBC reported on Friday, citing two former USDA officials.
The former official expressed concerns that hackers “could compromise the accuracy of the information that officers rely on.” AFP has contacted the FBI and USDA for comment.

stories.title: Wall Street ends sharply lower on AI selloff, S&P 500, Dow in correction
summary: US stocks extended their rout on Friday, and the S&P ​500 and the Dow both confirmed corrections after Anthropic’s momentous debut fell flat, exacerbating worries about the AI trade that has driven this year’s stock market rally.

Anthropic’s supersized debut as a publicly held company, which was intended to raise as much as $2 trillion in market cap, failed to catch ​fire on Thursday, closing 17.1pc above its $83 offer price as enthusiasm for the stock faded throughout the session.
In its second day as a publicly held company, Anthropic’s shares fell 9.1pc; Nvidia’s shares tumbled 13.8pc.

stories.title: Yemen’s Houthis launch strikes after Saudi coalition’s 'special operation'
summary: Yemen’s Houthis launched strikes on the Saudi capital Riyadh on Saturday, after vowing reprisals for a “special operation” by the Saudi-led coalition fighting them.

Saudi Arabia has been battling a surge in attacks since fighting reignited in neighbouring Yemen’s civil war this summer, where Riyadh backs the internationally recognised government against the Houthis.
The strikes came after the Houthis vowed revenge for the coalition’s attack on the Red Sea port city of Hodeida and other targets on Friday.

stories.title: Countries open path towards 'killer robots' pact
summary: Countries agreed on Saturday to open a path towards finding an international agreement on regulating lethal autonomous weapons systems, though campaigners seeking to stop so-called killer robots were disappointed by the “watered-down” outcome.

The 128 countries party to the CCW “agreed to launch the elaboration of an international instrument on lethal autonomous weapons systems, which should be conducted over the next two years”, conference president Julien Thoni told reporters afterwards.
While a majority of states went in favour of a legally binding agreement, countries that have the technology, including the United States and Russia, are reluctant to have their hands tied.

stories.title: Cummins wins Cricket Australia's 'unanimous support' to remain Test captain
summary: Cricket Australia threw its “unanimous support” behind Pat Cummins to remain Test captain Saturday, rejecting any suggestion his integrity had been compromised by the lingering “Sandpapergate” scandal.
Only then-captain Steve Smith, his deputy David Warner and Bancroft – who used the sandpaper – were found to be responsible by a Cricket Australia probe.

Otherwise, from this point, captaining the Australian team in Perth (at the first Test) will be my focus and priority.” Hazlewood threw his support behind Cummins earlier Saturday and made a veiled threat to call it a day if he was removed as captain.

stories.title: Court extends physical remand of accused in minor maid’s murder case in Islamabad
summary: Directs investigating officer to determine whether the child was subjected to bonded labour and exploitation The prosecution further informed the court that an electric iron had been recovered from the female accused and a stick from the male accused.

The court also ordered the IO to verify the alleged relationship between the complainant and the accused family, and to ascertain whether any actual arrangement regarding her education, maintenance, or welfare was made.
Furthermore, the court directed an inquiry into whether the child was engaged in domestic work or employed in any capacity, including any child labour or exploitation.

stories.title: Three suspects remanded into FIA custody over counterfeit vaccine in Islamabad
summary: The FIA had sought a 14-day physical remand of the suspects to investigate the alleged supply and administration of counterfeit vaccines.
The agency alleged that the suspects had administered substandard and counterfeit doses of Influvac Tetra vaccine, bearing lot number P13, to patients.
The FIA informed the court that reports issued by the Drug Regulatory Authority of Pakistan (Drap) and the Punjab government had declared the vaccine from the said lot counterfeit and substandard.

stories.title: Alarming rise in dog-bite cases echoes in Sindh Assembly
summary: KARACHI: The issue of an alarming rise in dog-bite cases echoed in the Sindh Assembly on Friday, with the government claiming that the process of catching stray dogs for vaccination is under way across the province.

Local Government Minister Syed Nasir Hussain Shah said that considerable work had been done on stray dogs, but more steps were needed. “The process of catching stray dogs, vaccinating them and releasing them again is under way in different areas of the province,” he added.
The minister said that a pilot project of the digital labour inspection system was under way in Karachi, and the labour department’s manual system was gradually being shifted online.

stories.title: Magistrate indicts anchorperson Iqrarul Hassan for cyberterrorism
summary: KARACHI: A judicial magistrate (East) on Friday framed charges against anchorperson Iqrarul Hassan in a case pertaining to cyberterrorism and the alleged dissemination of anti-state, false and defamatory content on his official social media accounts.

Last month, Mr Hassan was arrested by National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) at his home in Lahore in connection with a case registered in Karachi under multiple provisions of the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (Peca).

The NCCIA had registered a case against Mr Hassan for offences under Sections 9 (glorification of an offence), 10 (cyberterrorism), 20 (offences against dignity of a natural person), 24 (cyberstalking) and 26-A (punishment for false and fake information) of Peca.

stories.title: Alleged rapist of daughter killed in ‘CCD encounter’ in Kot Addu
summary: A case was registered against the suspect on the complaint of her grandmother on November 18.
Earlier, in July, a case was also registered against the suspect on the complaint of another woman for allegedly raping her but he was not arrested at the time.
A CCD spokesperson said that they were carrying the suspect to Qasba Gujrat when his three accomplices opened fire at them.

stories.title: Mobile phone explosion: Panicked passengers shatter windowpanes, door of e-bus in Bahawalpur
summary: BAHAWALPUR: Passengers travelling in an e-Green Bus got panicked here on Friday, with some of them shattering its windowpanes and door glass, and some others jumping out of the moving vehicle, after a mobile phone exploded in the bus near Dring Stadium.
As soon as he connected the charger’s wire to the port, the mobile phone exploded, filling the bus with smoke, they say.
The management also admitted that due to confusion and panic, passengers shattered four windowpanes, while a woman smashed the bus’ glass door in a bid to exit the vehicle.

stories.title: Minor boy suffers leg fracture ‘at employer’s hands’ in Lahore
summary: LAHORE: A minor boy working as a house help was hospitalised with a fractured leg and other serious injuries after he was allegedly subjected to brutal torture by his employer in Nawab Town here on Friday.

Perveen Bibi, the victim’s mother, told the police that her minor son was employed as a house help by the suspect, Hassan, who allegedly subjected the boy to inhuman torture with a club on theft allegations.
As a result the boy suffered multiple serious injuries, including a leg fracture, she alleged.

stories.title: Gujranwala, Multan overtake Lahore in air pollution
summary: The readings indicate a widespread deterioration in air quality across Punjab, with several cities experiencing hazardous pollution levels that pose serious health risks, particularly to children, elderly people and those suffering from respiratory and cardiovascular diseases.
During the critical smog period from Sept 1 to Nov 18, the department conducted 29,999 visits, demolished 519 kilns, sealed 494 and registered 408 FIRs, besides imposing fines totalling Rs101.45m.
In the first 18 days of November, enforcement teams conducted 7,509 visits, demolished 101 kilns, sealed 161 and registered 96 FIRs, while imposing fines totalling Rs27.6m.

stories.title: Before we design new provinces
summary: Article 239(4) further requires any bill altering a province’s limits to secure a two-thirds majority of that provincial assembly’s total membership before presidential assent.
A national majority through referendum may favour a change whose costs fall chiefly on the people of one particular province.
The question remains: can a referendum, by itself, effect the extensive constitutional changes that creating new provinces would entail?

stories.title: Balochistan CM promises jobs across the province
summary: QUETTA: Balochistan Chief Minister Mir Sarfraz Bugti has said that recruitment against vacant federal posts in the province will be extended to all districts in phases to ensure that people from across Balochistan benefit in proportion to their population.

Speaking during the provincial assembly session on Friday, MPA Engineer Zamarak Khan Achakzai, while raising a point of order, welcomed the federal government’s decision to initiate recruitment against vacant posts in 12 districts of Balochistan.

Responding to the concerns, Chief Minister Sarfraz Bugti thanked the president, the prime minister and the field marshal for initiating recruitment against vacant posts to provide employment opportunities to the youth of Balochistan.

stories.title: Pakistan rises 17 places in UN e-governance ranking
summary: Federal Minister for Inform­a­tion Technology and Telecom­m­unication Shaza Fatima Khawaja said: “Pakistan has risen 31 places in two editions of the UN’s benchmark for digital government.
Its score for online services increased by 20 per cent to 0.8422, the second-highest in Southern Asia, reflecting the growing availability of government services through digital channels.

He said the government would build on this progress in the next phase of the Digital Nation agenda, focusing on extending digital services, connectivity and digital skills to every part of the country.

stories.title: Fazl calls for transparent elections, criticises government over provincial rights
summary: Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman on Saturday called for transparent elections, saying they were necessary to address the country’s problems, while criticising the government over its handling of provincial rights, security and political affairs.
Fazl said his party was not against the military, describing it as the country’s defence force.
Fazl said his party welcomed investment in the country but alleged that those who opposed a particular narrative were threatened with the opening of cases against them.

stories.title: Australia gives Cummins unanimous backing as captain
summary: Cricket Australia (CA) backed Pat Cummins to remain as captain of the test and one-day international sides on Saturday and rejected any suggestion his integrity had ​been compromised amid the renewed furore over the 2018 ball-tampering incident.
"We've expressed our support to Pat and our ​concern for everyone impacted by the events of the 2018 tour of South Africa," ​Cricket Australia Chairman David Boon said in a statement.
Cummins welcomed the board's support and confirmed ​he would ⁠participate in the process.

stories.title: Pakistan, Indonesia conclude third edition of bilateral counter-terrorism exercise Elang Strike-III
summary: The Pakistan Army and Indonesian Army concluded the third edition of the bilateral counter-terrorism exercise, Elang Strike-III, at the National Counter Terrorism Centre (NCTC) in Pabbi, the military’s media wing said on Saturday.

According to the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), "the exercise focused on sharing counter-terrorism experiences, refining operational drills and procedures, and enhancing combat skills through mutual learning and the exchange of best practices".

On May 7, Pakistan and Sri Lanka concluded a two-week-long joint counter-terrorism exercise at Tarbela, focused on enhancing counter-terrorism skills and strengthening their longstanding military-to-military relations.

stories.title: Meta's India offices hit by opposition protests over account removals
summary: The youth wing of India's main opposition ​Congress party clashed with police outside Meta offices, protesting the company's removal of some Instagram accounts of its members, ‌according to footage released by the group on Saturday.
Debate is growing in India about potential risks to free speech from the increasingly strict efforts of Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government ​to remove social media content it objects to.
Congress has long accused Meta and other social ⁠media platforms of curbing dissent online by removing party accounts, favouring Modi's government.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia says it intercepts three Houthi missiles targeting Riyadh
summary: The Saudi-led coalition fighting Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis said on Saturday it had intercepted and destroyed three ballistic missiles fired towards Riyadh, marking the second Houthi attack on the Saudi capital in a few days, after its tallest skyscraper was struck on Thursday.

The latest attack followed an escalation in cross-border strikes on Friday, when the Saudi-led coalition said it had struck the Red Sea port of Hodeidah and carried out operations targeting Houthi missile and drone capabilities in the capital, Sanaa.

Separately, the army noted strikes on Friday by the Saudi-led coalition against facilities at the Hudaydah port in western Yemen and sites in the capital Sanaa that it said were being used by the Houthis to support military operations.

stories.title: India on top in first New Zealand Test
summary: KL Rahul made 136 and Shubman Gill 98 as India were 486-4 at the close of play Saturday in the first Test against New Zealand, a lead of 118 runs with two days remaining.
Kyle Jamieson was the best of New Zealand's bowlers taking 1-57, while Duffy ended the day with the fourth most expensive figures in New Zealand's Test history, with 1-180 from 29 overs.
India had resumed at 159-1 to start the day, a deficit of 209 runs, with Rahul on 52 and Padikkal on 16.

stories.title: Myanmar genocide judgment may bolster Gaza case against Israel
summary: South Africa, which has brought a genocide case against Israel over its conduct in Gaza, welcomed the judgment.
Read: Inside ICJ's historic Rohingya genocide ruling against Myanmar Both Myanmar and Israel have defended the actions of their armed forces as legitimate responses to insurgencies.
Important Precedent Israeli legal scholar Yuval Shany said the ruling could broaden the arguments available to South Africa in its case against Israel.

stories.title: New caravan of about 300 migrants crosses into southern Mexico
summary: A caravan of about 300 migrants, mostly from Central America, crossed into southern Mexico on Friday to join a larger group heading north, a week after United States President Donald Trump threatened fresh tariffs on Mexico if it did not halt the movement.

Read: Trump's personalised diplomacy hits its limits with 3-way summit "We’ve thought about staying in Mexico to work, until Donald Trump leaves office," said Herson David Escalante, a Honduran national, as he walked as part of the new caravan.
Last week, Trump threatened to double tariffs on goods from Mexico if its authorities did not stop the caravan.

stories.title: Iraq fire at Basra power station kills at least four, injures 30
summary: At least 4 people were killed and 30 injured in a fire at a power station in southern Iraq on Saturday, with the toll expected to rise, security officials said.
Civil defence teams brought the fire at the Hartha power station north of Basra under control after firefighters responded to the incident, Iraq's state news agency, INA, reported.
The fire spread to neighbouring houses and forced operations at the power station to stop, the security officials said.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz condemns Houthi attack on Riyadh’s King Abdullah Financial District
summary: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Saturday strongly condemned the Houthi attack on the King Abdullah Financial District in Riyadh, describing it as an act of “reckless aggression” targeting civilian infrastructure and economic facilities.

The latest attack followed an escalation in cross-border strikes on Friday, when the Saudi-led coalition said it had struck the Red Sea port of Hodeidah and carried out operations targeting Houthi missile and drone capabilities in the capital, Sanaa.

On October 26, Pakistan strongly condemned "reprehensible" Houthi ballistic missile attacks on October 24, which had targeted the Makkah and Madinah regions of Saudi Arabia, including areas in the vicinity of the holy sites.

stories.title: Tanker hit by unknown projectile near Oman's Khasab, UKMTO says
summary: Read: Probe points to possible US role in Iran school strike A UN-backed fact-finding mission recently said there were reasonable grounds to believe that the US had committed war crimes in the two Tomahawk airstrikes in Iran, including one that struck the school in Minab.
Separately, the US State Department said that the four designated individuals illicitly sell oil to help fund Iran's military and its support for terrorism.

Trump, in a press conference on Friday, said: "They want to make a deal, but they don't want to make a deal that's acceptable to me." The United States and Israel attacked Iran on February 28, prompting Tehran to retaliate against Israel and Gulf states hosting US military bases.

stories.title: Mechanically unfit traffic police vehicles barred from Pindi roads
summary: RAWALPINDI: Mechanically unfit police vehicles will not be allowed to operate on Rawalpindi roads and departmental action will be taken against drivers found negligent in their maintenance.
Drivers to face action over negligence, improper maintenance Presently, there are 45 vehicles, including fork-lifters, and 550 motorcycles in the fleet of the Rawalpindi traffic police.
During the inspection of 15 vehicles on Friday in the first phase, three vehicles, including two fork-lifters, were found emitting smoke and mechanically unfit.

stories.title: Security to be stepped up for Sikh pilgrims visiting Punja Sahib
summary: The plan includes installation of walkthrough gates, surveillance cameras, searchlights and layered security cordons around key entry and exit points.
Walkthrough gates and around 50 security cameras have been installed at the gurdwara, while 40 metal detectors and luggage scanners have been placed at entry points to ensure strict monitoring.

Speaking on this occasion, Dr Mudassir Ahmed Shah said that all arrangements, including security, transport and accommodation, have been finalised to ensure that pilgrims can perform their religious obligations in a peaceful and dignified environment.

stories.title: JUI-F leaders being targeted for refusing to join govt: Fazl
summary: Mr Fazl said that in Punjab, authorities were pressuring JUI-F workers and leaders to quit the party but not a single activist was willing to abandon the party anywhere in the country.
He claimed that the Mufti Mehmood Markaz was not an encroachment. “Our Markaz is not an encroachment.

What business do they have in Pakistan’s politics?” The JUI-F leader alleged that authorities were “stealing” Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s mineral resources and had become angry when his party exposed the theft.

stories.title: Education dept restricts media access to govt schools in Charsadda
summary: The decision comes as journalists in different districts of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa are highlighting the deteriorating condition of public-sector educational institutions, including overcrowded classrooms and a lack of essential facilities.
At Government Primary School Paindakhel, around 380 students are enrolled, but the institution has only three classrooms, forcing many children to attend lessons in the open.
Similarly, Government Primary School Majoki has more than 300 students but only five classrooms.

stories.title: Three die as vehicle falls in Panjkora River
summary: Rescue 1122 and police personnel rushed to the scene.
Rescue personnel recovered a large amount of cash from the belongings of a deceased and handed over the money to his heirs.

Residents and the bereaved families praised the rescue personnel for their honesty and sense of duty, saying their conduct reflected that the rescuers considered safeguarding people’s belongings, alongside saving lives, an important part of their responsibility.

stories.title: Young woman, man shot dead for ‘honour’ in Oghi
summary: Oghi SHO Amir Khan told reporters that the suspect, whose family had shifted to Oghi from Kohistan, killed his young daughter and the man for honour.

AFGHANS DETAINED: Police have arrested more than 350 Afghan nationals staying illegally in different parts of the district over the past three weeks and handed them over to the district administration for deportation to their homeland.

He said that earlier Afghan nationals settled anywhere in the district were arrested and booked under Section 14 of the Foreigners Act, 1946, but now they were taken into custody and handed over to the district administration for their own deportation to their home country.

stories.title: PHC directs govt to notify recruitment rules for NCCIA within three months
summary: PESHAWAR: The Peshawar High Court has directed the federal government to finalise the service and recruitment rules for the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) within three months.
The court directed the government and other respondents, including the NCCIA director general, not to take any adverse action against the petitioners until the rules were notified.
Meanwhile, the respondents initiated fresh recruitment and deputation against cybercrime-related posts instead of regularising the petitioners.

stories.title: Provinces cannot assume ‘unexercised’ federal powers: FCC
summary: The FCC observed that the impugned judgements had given controlling weight to the infrastructure purpose, movement of goods and asserted compensatory character of the cess without first establishing provincial legislative competence.

The FCC further observed that the abolition of the Concurrent Legislative List through the 18th Amendment had expanded provincial competence but had not transferred subjects expressly retained in the federal domain.

During the hearing, the taxpayers had contended that the levies encroached upon parliament’s exclusive legislative domain and could not be sustained as fees or compensatory charges merely because the goods used provincial infrastructure.
